items.headline: High Surf Advisory issued October 24 at 9:42PM EDT until October 26 at 5:00PM EDT by NWS Charleston SC
items.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 4
to 7 feet in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk,
dangerous rip currents. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, up to
one foot of inundation above ground level expected along
shorelines and tidal waterways (10.0 to 10.2 feet Mean Lower
Low Water at Fort Pulaski).

* WHERE...In Georgia, Coastal Bryan, Coastal Chatham, Coastal
Liberty and Coastal McIntosh Counties. In South Carolina,
Beaufort and Coastal Jasper Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 5 PM EDT Monday. For
the High Rip Current Risk, through Sunday evening. For the
Coastal Flood Advisory, from 5 AM to 10 AM EDT Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Saltwater inundation will impact some roads.
Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach
erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tide will occur around 7:44 AM
Sunday at Fort Pulaski. Saltwater inundation will be possible
1 to 2 hours before and after high tide.
items.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Visit water.weather.gov for additional water level and flood
impact information.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

items.headline: Gale Warning issued October 24 at 2:17PM EDT until October 26 at 5:00AM EDT by NWS Charleston SC
items.description:
* WHAT...Northeast winds 25 to 35 kt with gusts up to 40 kt and
seas 6 to 11 ft.

* WHERE...Edisto Beach to Savannah out 20 NM.

* WHEN...Until 5 AM EDT Monday.

* IMPACTS...Strong winds will cause hazardous seas which could
capsize or damage vessels and reduce visibility.
items.instruction:
Mariners should alter plans to avoid these hazardous conditions.
Remain in port, seek safe harbor, alter course, and/or secure the
vessel for hazardous conditions.
